steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The criminal justice system involves: police (investigate), CPS (prosecute), courts (try), sentencing (punish), probation (supervise in community), prison (custodial sentences).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The police are responsible for preventing and detecting crime, maintaining public order, and protecting life and property. Police officers have powers of arrest, stop and search, and detention.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) reviews evidence gathered by the police and decides whether to charge — applying the Full Code Test (sufficient evidence + public interest).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Trial by jury is available for serious criminal offences ('indictable offences') in the Crown Court. The jury of 12 citizens decides the verdict; the judge decides the sentence.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the roles of different criminal justice agencies: police → CPS → courts → probation/prison When evaluating sentencing, consider all four purposes: punishment, deterrence, rehabilitation, protection Use statistics where possible — e.g. 46% reoffending rate — to support evaluation
